Question 2(c) [4 marks]: How could government policies affect operations management?

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
4 marks: Clearly details cause and effect of government policies on operations with a definition and two impacts
2–3 marks: Details cause and effect of government policies on operations with reference to one impact, may include a definition
1 marks: Defines government policy or outlines an impact on operations management


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Government policies are methods used by the government to influence the economic and social conditions of the economy. They can impose a cost or create a benefit and are outside management's control. Policies are often directed at inputs such as electricity and labour, usually to increase efficiency and reduce cost; they may influence which inputs are used (subsidies for solar, R&D grants), encourage certain outputs (subsidies to car manufacturers, keeping associated part manufacturers alive, as with Holden in Elizabeth SA), and affect the quantity of output through their impact on economic growth, government spending and interest rates (which can defer spending on equipment upgrades).
